which is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for applicant, Mr. Ankit Mishra, learned counsel for applicant no. 2,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.
3. By means of the present application under Section 528 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
Bilal Ahmad ( A.B.. Ahmad ) vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ...

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25688949/
1 2023 (482 Cr.P.C.) the applicants have sought following prayer:-
"to quash the non-bailable warrant order dated 29.03.2023 issued against the applicants in Criminal Case No. 1719 of 2022 (State Vs. Ankish Bilal Ahamd) arising out of Case Crime No. 265 of 2021 under Sections 406, 420, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Sitapur pending before learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sitapur."
4. Learned counsel for applicant, after arguing at some length submits that grievance of the applicant shall be redressed in case liberty is granted to the applicant to file a bail application which may be decided in view of law laid down by Supreme Court in "Satender Kumar Antil versus Central Bureau of Investigation and another, Special Leave to Appeal (Cri)No.5191 of 2021" to which learned A.G.A. has no objection.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil versus Central Bureau of Investigation and another, Special Leave to Appeal (Cri)No.5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. In view of the above, prayer for quashing the impugned proceeding is refused.

So far as other prayer is concerned, it is provided that in case the applicant appears before the trial court within two weeks from today and applies for bail, the same shall be decided expeditiously, in view of the law laid down by Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil's case (supra).
6.
The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed of accordingly.
